title: Your Model Already Knows: Attention-Guided Safety Filter for Vision-Language-Action Models
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (attention read from action-query to vision-key block of layer 12, head 3)
methods: per-head attention profiling on 4 episodes with ground-truth targets to pick a target-localizing head
attention density per tracked object over a sliding window with a decisive-gap rule
separating-hyperplane CBF-QP safety filter on the end-effector ellipsoid
question: Can a VLA's own attention heads identify the object it is acting toward at every step, so a CBF safety filter can treat everything else as an obstacle in dynamic scenes?
key_findings: Only a few heads carry target-identification signal; layer-wise averages peak at layer 12 (then layer 8) for both cameras; layer 12 head 3 is used for all suites.

SafeLIBERO Level III (adversarially moving obstacle): KNOWS vs Naive init-only filter safe-success 54.5 vs 34.0 (Spatial), 70.5 vs 40.0 (Object), 63.5 vs 9.5 (Goal), 34.5 vs 18.5 (Long); collision rate 29.0 vs 62.0, 14.0 vs 50.0, 30.5 vs 90.5, 34.0 vs 80.5 (the 'about 43%' average reduction).

Static levels I-II: KNOWS is comparable or worse than the privileged Naive filter (e.g. Spatial I SSR 53.0 vs 61.0, Long II 24.0 vs 42.5), and far better than no filter (unfiltered collision rates 64.5-95.0%).
Overhead: attention extraction 0.8 ms, target identification 9.4 ms, QP 11.4 ms, segmentation 19.3 ms; wrapper total 49.3 ms within the 20 Hz budget.

Passively recorded attention predicts success on 80 LIBERO-Long episodes (44 success / 36 failure): early-window target density AUC 0.89 (whole episode 0.70), early target mass AUC 0.93; density on the not-yet-relevant destination is at chance (AUC 0.55).

benchmarks: SafeLIBERO Spatial, Object, Goal, Long at levels I-II (static) and new level III (dynamic obstacle)
evidence.scale: 50 episodes per task; head selection from 4 profiling episodes; success-prediction analysis on 80 episodes
evidence.statistics: no tests or CIs on SR/CR/SSR; AUCs reported without CIs
evidence.baselines: no CBF; 'Naive' filter with one ground-truth obstacle ellipsoid placed at t = 0 and never updated (stand-in for VLM-based init-only filters)

causal_validation: No interpretability claim is tested causally: attention is used as a read-out, and the destination-vs-target AUC contrast is a specificity check, not an intervention. Crucially there is no ablation that isolates the attention signal from per-step object tracking.
closed_loop: Yes, safety results are closed-loop rollouts with the filter active; the success-prediction AUCs come from passively recorded closed-loop episodes.
limitations_stated: Only the end-effector ellipsoid is protected; arm links can still collide.
Perception errors (point-cloud noise, tracker mis-association) cause conservative behavior or collisions.
Safety holds on the reduced-order end-effector model only up to the operational-space controller's tracking error; the CBF is a practical margin, not a certificate.
A weaker backbone may yield diffuse attention and a worse filter.
critique: The Level III gain is confounded: KNOWS re-tracks every object every step while the Naive baseline places a single obstacle once. A tracker-plus-oracle-target or tracker-plus-random-target ablation is needed to credit the attention head.

The head is selected on 4 episodes from one suite using ground-truth targets, then reused everywhere; no check of how often the attention-chosen target is correct per step is reported in the text read.
Single model (pi0.5), simulation only, no statistics; Long-suite results are weak for all methods.

The finding that a target-specific head in the action expert's attention predicts success (AUC 0.89) fits the failure-prediction literature and shows attention can carry task-relevant signal, but it is correlational.
one_line: Reads one attention head of pi0.5 to find the object the policy is reaching for, treats every other tracked object as an obstacle in a CBF filter, and cuts collisions with moving obstacles in SafeLIBERO, though the gain is not separated from simply tracking objects every step.
